scope: Independent preimplementation review for testability, fixed behavioral oracles, original-source preservation, and evidence limits. This record approves the test plan only; the separate plan-review record is still required before implementation.

basis: The plan retains B02's FastAPI/PostgreSQL user API, command/outbox acceptance, and per-request workspace scope, with B03 Temporal as a separate transition authority.

It preserves original DTOs and the ax_session boundary, identifies the added login/session routes and pagination as implementation additions, and explicitly keeps the entire AT-21 job/log/image/device direct-resource matrix pending until the later endpoints exist.
Paperclip identity and company membership are not promoted to IFPMIC authority; synthetic provider, workspace, and profile fixtures are explicitly not real SSO, approval, or AT-21 evidence.

The plan fixes subject identity, session and CSRF lifetime, cookie attributes, routes, DTOs, status/error codes, request limits, idempotency behavior, DRAFT/accepted semantics, and resource authorization policy sufficiently for independent literal HTTP/DB assertions.

G2 provides byte-level B01 bridge checks for exact framing, record hash, identity, Unicode/lone-surrogate transport, limits, timeout, and private-data non-disclosure without asking Python to reproduce the JavaScript canonicalizer.

G3/G4 specify wrong/replayed OIDC state, nonce and PKCE, identity spoofing, expiry/revocation, membership/delegation, cross-user reads, idempotency races, transaction rollback, commit uncertainty, and pagination scope cases.
G5 names concrete filesystem crash/fault points, real directory/marker checks, symlink and unexpected-content rejection, stale-claim behavior, and recovery expectations.
The app factory and private fault hooks provide test seams while requiring actual PostgreSQL, independent connections/processes, and actual temporary filesystem checks for acceptance evidence.
The 180-second G6 command limit has an explicit prior 120-second runtime rationale; shorter protocol/fault and Python command limits remain separately stated.

The UI/browser gate omission rule is conditional on unchanged UI/build/plugin/dependency outputs and no frontend integration; backend identity, PostgreSQL, bridge, and workspace tests are never omitted.
Real corporate OIDC, production TLS/proxy, production database/backups, workspace policy, Temporal, B04/B09, and all unexecuted ATs remain clearly outside the synthetic local acceptance claim.

nonblocking_test_execution_constraints.constraint: Provisioning remains outside the user-facing CreateJob API and production eligibility/grant authority remains an environment acceptance item. Tests may use explicit isolated PostgreSQL fixtures for active membership, job ownership/delegation, and profile eligibility, but must assert the plan's fixed authorization behavior and must not imply that a real operator provisioning interface or approval source was delivered.

Use the configured synthetic issuer/client/redirect as the independent fixture oracle. Assert callback state is browser-bound, single-use within five minutes; nonce, PKCE S256, issuer, audience/client, azp when present/required by the configured provider, signature algorithm/key, exp and nbf failures are rejected. Concurrent/replayed consumption must not create more than one authenticated session. Fixture success is not corporate SSO acceptance.

Assert stable `(created_at, job_id)` continuation, tamper rejection, actor/filter binding, and per-page reauthorization without pinning a private token encoding. Invalid cursor input should use the plan's fixed INVALID_REQUEST contract; no cross-user cursor may reveal a protected row.

For commit-response loss and workspace crash tests, preserve the original failure attempt and re-read with a new connection/process. A 202/accepted receipt is never counted as applied or workspace READY; synthetic recovery is not B03 dispatch or AT-21 completion.

material_blockers.evidence: docs/ifpmic/design-v1/specs/openapi.v1.json#/components/schemas/Job requires workflow_version. docs/ifpmic/B01-PROFILES.md states that Job.workflow_version maps to the immutable registry ID and identifies the registry workflow_id as ifpmic-sw-v1. The B02 DRAFT insert tuple at PostgreSQL request acceptance lists revision, cycle, current_step_ids, and candidate_fingerprint but omits workflow_version and its binding.
material_blockers.why_material: A successful CreateJob cannot produce a complete original Job DTO without this required value, and the independently expected registry binding cannot be tested from the current plan. Treating schema_version or profile_version as workflow_version would violate the adjacent B01 contract.
material_blockers.required_plan_resolution: Pin the initial and returned Job.workflow_version to the exact B01 immutable registry ID (ifpmic-sw-v1), distinguish it from profile_version and schema_version, and add a literal API/DB assertion for the value.

material_blockers.topic: Unicode validity for persisted CreateJob strings
material_blockers.evidence: The plan rejects lone-surrogate project_id values and separately defines lossless ASCII-escaped storage for B01 profile_version, but CreateJob also accepts title, request_text, and base_ref strings and persists command/job-related data in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL UTF8 text cannot store lone UTF-16 surrogates. The current per-field rules do not specify whether such values are rejected or preserved.
material_blockers.why_material: A valid JSON body can encode a lone surrogate with an escape. Without a pinned policy, the same input may become an uncaught database encoding failure, be silently changed, or be inconsistently accepted by API and digest code; TC has no independent status/round-trip oracle.
material_blockers.required_plan_resolution: For every user-controlled string persisted as PostgreSQL text, either reject non-Unicode-scalar strings as INVALID_REQUEST before transaction start or define lossless escaped storage and response behavior. Preserve ordinary astral characters and do not normalize. Add escaped-lone-surrogate and astral-string tests for the chosen rule.
